subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: Conductors and Insulators: Materials in Electrical Circuits
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Science strand: a conductor allows electric current to flow easily through it, while an insulator resists the flow of electric current, a property that shapes how circuits and everyday devices are designed.

quiz.q: A conductor is a material that ___.
options: Blocks electric current from flowing through it
Allows electric current to flow through it easily
A concept unrelated to conductors
Has no connection to electricity at all

quiz.q: An insulator is a material that ___.
options: A concept unrelated to insulators
Resists the flow of electric current
Allows electric current to flow through it easily
Always conducts electricity better than metal

quiz.q: Which of these materials is typically a good conductor of electricity?
options: A material unrelated to conducting electricity
Rubber
Plastic
Copper

quiz.q: Why is rubber often used to coat electrical wires?
options: A reason unrelated to electrical safety
Rubber has no effect on how a wire functions
It insulates the wire, helping prevent electric shock
It conducts electricity better than the metal wire inside

quiz.q: Why is it important to understand the difference between conductors and insulators when designing electrical devices?
options: It helps ensure electricity flows where intended and people stay safe from shock
A reason unrelated to electrical safety
All materials conduct electricity in exactly the same way
This distinction has no effect on how devices are designed

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: Levels of Government in Canada: Municipal, Provincial, Federal
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Social Studies strand: Canada’s government is organized into three levels — municipal, provincial, and federal — each with distinct responsibilities for serving citizens.

quiz.q: Canada’s government is organized into which three levels?
options: Only a single level, with no other divisions
Regional, continental, and global
Municipal, provincial, and federal
A concept unrelated to Canada’s government structure

quiz.q: Which level of government is typically responsible for services like local roads and garbage collection?
options: Municipal government
Federal government
A level unrelated to these responsibilities
A level of government that does not exist in Canada

quiz.q: Which level of government is responsible for national defence and issues like immigration policy?
options: Federal government
Municipal government
A level of government that does not exist in Canada
A level unrelated to these responsibilities

quiz.q: Which level of government typically oversees education and healthcare policy within a province?
options: No level of government oversees these areas
Provincial government
A level unrelated to these responsibilities
Municipal government only

quiz.q: Why does Canada divide responsibilities among three levels of government?
options: Dividing responsibilities serves no practical purpose
It allows different levels to focus on issues suited to local, regional, or national scale
A single level of government could handle every responsibility identically well
A reason unrelated to Canada’s government structure

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Oral Communication: Active Listening and Note-Taking
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Language strand: active listening involves fully focusing on a speaker and responding thoughtfully, while effective note-taking captures key ideas concisely rather than every single word.

quiz.q: Active listening involves ___.
options: Only hearing a speaker while thinking about something else
A concept unrelated to active listening
Interrupting a speaker as often as possible
Fully focusing on a speaker and responding thoughtfully

quiz.q: Effective notes should generally capture ___.
options: Key ideas concisely, rather than every single word
A concept unrelated to note-taking
Every single word a speaker says, with nothing left out
Only the speaker’s name, with no other information

quiz.q: Which of these is a sign of active listening?
options: Looking away and checking a phone during a conversation
Talking over the speaker repeatedly
Making eye contact and nodding to show understanding
A behaviour unrelated to active listening

quiz.q: Why might using abbreviations and symbols be helpful while taking notes?
options: They can help a listener record information quickly without missing key points
Abbreviations always make notes harder to understand later
A reason unrelated to note-taking
Using symbols is never useful while taking notes

quiz.q: Why is active listening an important skill in both school and everyday life?
options: A reason unrelated to oral communication
It helps build understanding, respect, and clear communication with others
Listening skills are not connected to understanding a speaker
Active listening has no real benefit in communication

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Solving Equations Involving Decimals
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Math strand: solving equations involving decimals uses the same inverse-operation steps as whole-number equations, applied carefully to decimal values.

quiz.q: To solve an equation with a decimal, you generally ___.
options: Ignore the decimal point during the solving process
A method unrelated to solving equations
Round every decimal to zero before solving
Use inverse operations, just as with whole numbers

quiz.q: Solve for x: x + 2.5 = 7.8.
options: A solution unrelated to the equation

quiz.q: Solve for x: x - 1.4 = 3.6.
options: A solution unrelated to the equation

quiz.q: Solve for x: 2x = 9.4.
options: A solution unrelated to the equation

quiz.q: Why is it important to keep decimal points aligned while solving these equations?
options: A reason unrelated to solving equations
Misaligned decimals can make the answer’s place value incorrect
Decimal point placement never affects the accuracy of an answer
Decimal points can be placed anywhere without changing the value

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: Drones and Modern Flight Technology
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Science strand: drones are unpiloted aircraft controlled remotely or by onboard computers, using propellers and the same basic forces of flight as other aircraft.

quiz.q: A drone is best described as ___.
options: A concept unrelated to drones
An unpiloted aircraft controlled remotely or by onboard computers
A type of boat used for water travel
An aircraft that must always have a pilot inside it

quiz.q: Like other aircraft, drones rely on which force to overcome gravity?
options: Friction only
A force unrelated to flight
Lift
Density

quiz.q: Which of these is a common real-world use for drones today?
options: Underwater exploration only, never aerial tasks
Drones have no practical uses
Aerial photography and package delivery
A use unrelated to drone technology

quiz.q: How do most small drones typically generate lift?
options: Large fixed wings alone, with no propellers
A method unrelated to how drones fly
Spinning propellers that push air downward
Balloons filled with helium

quiz.q: Why might drones be useful for scientists studying hard-to-reach environments?
options: They can access and capture data from locations that are difficult or unsafe for people to reach
Drones can only be used in easily accessible locations
A reason unrelated to drone technology
Drones have no useful application in scientific research

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: How Canadians Vote: Elections and Political Parties
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Social Studies strand: Canadians participate in democracy by voting in elections for candidates who often represent political parties with differing platforms and ideas.

quiz.q: In a Canadian election, citizens generally vote for ___.
options: Only the Prime Minister directly, with no other candidates involved
A concept unrelated to Canadian elections
No one, since Canada does not hold elections
A candidate to represent their area, often as part of a political party

quiz.q: A political party is best described as ___.
options: A celebration with no connection to government
A group of people with similar political ideas who run candidates for office
A single individual with no supporters
A concept unrelated to elections

quiz.q: Why might citizens compare political party platforms before voting?
options: To choose the candidate or party whose ideas best match their own views
A reason unrelated to elections
All political parties always have identical platforms
Platforms have no influence on how people decide to vote

quiz.q: To be eligible to vote in a Canadian federal election, a citizen must generally be at least ___.
options: 30 years old
An age unrelated to voting eligibility
18 years old
10 years old

quiz.q: Why is voting considered an important part of Canadian democracy?
options: Elections are decided with no input from citizens at all
A reason unrelated to democracy
It gives citizens a voice in choosing their government representatives
Voting has no effect on who represents citizens in government

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Writing: Crafting Realistic Dialogue in Narrative
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Language strand: realistic dialogue reflects how people actually speak, reveals character personality, and follows proper punctuation conventions like quotation marks and new paragraphs for each speaker.

quiz.q: Realistic dialogue in a story should ___.
options: Avoid revealing anything about a character’s personality
Sound as formal as a textbook at all times
Reflect how people actually speak
A concept unrelated to dialogue

quiz.q: In written dialogue, a new paragraph is typically started ___.
options: A concept unrelated to dialogue formatting
Only once per entire conversation
After every single word that is spoken
Each time the speaker changes

quiz.q: Which of these correctly punctuates a line of dialogue?
options: I am ready to go, said Maya.
“I am ready to go,” said Maya.
“I am ready to go said Maya.
A sentence unrelated to dialogue punctuation

quiz.q: Why might a writer use dialogue to reveal a character’s personality?
options: A reason unrelated to writing dialogue
Only narration, never dialogue, can reveal character traits
The way a character speaks can show their attitude, background, or emotions
Dialogue never reveals anything about a character

quiz.q: Why is it important for dialogue to sound natural rather than overly formal?
options: Natural dialogue helps make characters and scenes feel realistic and relatable
The way characters speak has no effect on how readers experience a story
Formal dialogue always makes a story feel more realistic
A reason unrelated to writing dialogue

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Time: Elapsed Time and the 24-Hour Clock
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Math strand: elapsed time is the amount of time that passes between a start and an end time, and the 24-hour clock expresses time using hours 00 to 23 without needing a.m. or p.m.

quiz.q: Elapsed time is best described as ___.
options: The amount of time that passes between a start time and an end time
The exact time an event begins, with no reference to when it ends
A measurement that has nothing to do with clocks
A concept unrelated to elapsed time

quiz.q: On the 24-hour clock, 3:00 p.m. is written as ___.
options: A time unrelated to the conversion

quiz.q: If a movie starts at 14:30 and lasts 2 hours, at what time does it end?
options: A time unrelated to the calculation

quiz.q: How much time passes between 9:15 a.m. and 11:45 a.m.?
options: 2 hours 30 minutes
3 hours 15 minutes
2 hours
A duration unrelated to the calculation

quiz.q: Why might the 24-hour clock be useful for schedules like train or flight timetables?
options: It can only display times before noon
It avoids confusion between morning and afternoon times
The 24-hour clock makes timetables more confusing to read
A reason unrelated to timekeeping

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: The Layers of Earth’s Atmosphere
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Science strand: Earth’s atmosphere is made up of distinct layers, including the troposphere and stratosphere, each with different characteristics that support weather, climate, and life.

quiz.q: The layer of the atmosphere closest to Earth’s surface, where most weather occurs, is the ___.
options: Mesosphere
A layer unrelated to Earth’s atmosphere
Stratosphere
Troposphere

quiz.q: The stratosphere contains a layer that protects life on Earth by absorbing ___.
options: All visible light from the Sun
Sound waves travelling through space
Harmful ultraviolet radiation from the Sun
A concept unrelated to the stratosphere

quiz.q: Why does temperature generally decrease as altitude increases within the troposphere?
options: Temperature always increases the higher you travel through the troposphere
The troposphere has no connection to temperature at all
A reason unrelated to atmospheric layers
The air becomes thinner and less able to trap heat near the surface

quiz.q: Which gas makes up the largest percentage of Earth’s atmosphere?
options: A gas unrelated to Earth’s atmosphere
Nitrogen
Oxygen
Carbon dioxide

quiz.q: Why is it useful for scientists to study the different layers of the atmosphere?
options: A reason unrelated to Earth science
Earth’s atmosphere is a single uniform layer with no distinct sections
It helps explain weather patterns, climate, and how the atmosphere protects life on Earth
The atmosphere’s layers have no effect on weather or climate

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: The Role of the Governor General and Constitutional Monarchy
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Social Studies strand: Canada is a constitutional monarchy, meaning the monarch is head of state, represented in Canada by the Governor General, while elected officials hold governing power.

quiz.q: Canada is best described politically as a ___.
options: Absolute monarchy with no elected officials
Constitutional monarchy
Country with no head of state at all
A concept unrelated to Canada’s political structure

quiz.q: In Canada, the monarch is represented domestically by the ___.
options: A role unrelated to representing the monarch
Governor General
Prime Minister
Provincial premier

quiz.q: In a constitutional monarchy like Canada, who holds the actual governing power?
options: The monarch alone, with no elected input
No one holds any governing power
Elected officials, such as the Prime Minister and Parliament
A concept unrelated to constitutional monarchy

quiz.q: Which of these is a duty commonly associated with the Governor General?
options: A duty unrelated to the Governor General’s role
Replacing the Prime Minister whenever they choose
Formally giving royal assent to new laws passed by Parliament
Personally writing and voting on every new law

quiz.q: Why might Canada’s system be described as balancing tradition with democratic government?
options: It keeps a ceremonial monarchy while giving real governing power to elected representatives
It removes all connection between Canada and the monarchy
A reason unrelated to Canada’s political structure
It gives the monarch complete control over all governing decisions

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Reading: Identifying Text Structure Patterns
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Language strand: nonfiction texts are often organized using structure patterns such as sequence, cause and effect, compare and contrast, or problem and solution, and recognizing these patterns supports comprehension.

quiz.q: Recognizing a text’s structure pattern can help a reader ___.
options: Ignore the content of the text entirely
Only understand the title of a text
A concept unrelated to text structure
Better understand how ideas in the text are organized and connected

quiz.q: Which structure pattern presents events in the order they happened?
options: Compare and contrast
Problem and solution
Sequence
A pattern unrelated to text structure

quiz.q: A text organized using the compare and contrast pattern focuses on ___.
options: Only the order in which events occurred
A single cause with no described effect
A concept unrelated to text structure
Similarities and differences between two or more things

quiz.q: Which structure pattern would most likely be used in a text describing a challenge and how it was resolved?
options: Problem and solution
Compare and contrast
A pattern unrelated to text structure
Sequence only, with no described challenge

quiz.q: Why might recognizing a cause and effect structure help a reader understand a nonfiction article?
options: Cause and effect structures provide no useful information to readers
A reason unrelated to text structure
Recognizing structure patterns never improves comprehension
It helps clarify why something happened and what resulted from it

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Stem-and-Leaf Plots
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Math strand: a stem-and-leaf plot organizes numerical data by splitting each value into a stem (leading digit or digits) and a leaf (the final digit), keeping the original values visible.

quiz.q: In a stem-and-leaf plot, the stem usually represents ___.
options: The final digit of a value only
The total number of data points collected
A concept unrelated to stem-and-leaf plots
The leading digit or digits of a value

quiz.q: In a stem-and-leaf plot, the leaf usually represents ___.
options: The final digit of a value
The average of all the data
The leading digit of a value
A concept unrelated to stem-and-leaf plots

quiz.q: In the data value 47, which digit would typically be the leaf?
options: A digit unrelated to this value

quiz.q: What is one advantage of a stem-and-leaf plot compared to a simple list of numbers?
options: It can only be used with exactly two data points
It hides the original data values completely
A reason unrelated to stem-and-leaf plots
It organizes data by size while still showing every original value

quiz.q: Why might a teacher use a stem-and-leaf plot to display a class’s test scores?
options: Stem-and-leaf plots cannot be used to display test scores
It shows the spread and clustering of scores while keeping each score visible
It removes all individual scores from the display
A reason unrelated to data management

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: Insects and Pollinators: Their Role in Ecosystems
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Science strand: insects, including many pollinators like bees and butterflies, play essential roles in ecosystems by helping plants reproduce and supporting food webs.

quiz.q: Pollinators help plants reproduce by ___.
options: Removing pollen from flowers with no further effect
Carrying pollen from one flower to another
A concept unrelated to pollination
Preventing flowers from producing seeds

quiz.q: Which of these is a well-known pollinator?
options: A cloud
An organism unrelated to pollination
A bee
A rock

quiz.q: Why are many fruits and vegetables dependent on pollinators?
options: Fruits and vegetables never require pollination
Pollinators have no connection to fruit or vegetable production
A reason unrelated to pollinators
Pollination is often necessary for these plants to produce fruit and seeds

quiz.q: Besides pollination, how else do insects support many ecosystems?
options: Insects only exist outside of any food web
Insects provide no useful role to other organisms
They serve as an important food source for birds, amphibians, and other animals
A reason unrelated to ecosystems

quiz.q: Why might a decline in pollinator populations concern scientists?
options: It could reduce plant reproduction and disrupt food webs that depend on those plants
A reason unrelated to insects and ecosystems
A decline in pollinators would have no effect on ecosystems
Pollinators have no connection to the plants around them

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: Canada’s Justice System: Courts and the Rule of Law
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Social Studies strand: the rule of law means everyone, including government leaders, must follow the law, and Canada’s court system interprets and applies laws fairly through an independent judiciary.

quiz.q: The rule of law means that ___.
options: Laws apply differently depending on a person’s job
A concept unrelated to the rule of law
Everyone, including government leaders, must follow the law
Only ordinary citizens must follow the law, not leaders

quiz.q: Why is it important for Canada’s judges to be independent from political influence?
options: Judges are expected to always favour the government’s position
A reason unrelated to Canada’s justice system
It helps ensure fair and unbiased decisions in court cases
Judicial independence has no effect on the fairness of court decisions

quiz.q: Which of these is a role of Canada’s court system?
options: Interpreting and applying laws to resolve disputes and legal cases
A role unrelated to the court system
Writing new laws with no involvement from Parliament
Collecting taxes from citizens

quiz.q: What is the highest court in Canada, with the final say on legal appeals?
options: A court unrelated to Canada’s justice system
A provincial legislature
The Supreme Court of Canada
A municipal court

quiz.q: Why is the rule of law considered essential to a fair and functioning democracy?
options: A fair society can function without any laws at all
A reason unrelated to democracy
The rule of law has no connection to fairness in society
It ensures laws are applied consistently and that no one is above them

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Review: Language Days 61-69
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Language strand: this review lesson revisits key ideas from Days 61-69, including prepositional phrases, descriptive writing, fact versus opinion, prefixes and suffixes, and text structure patterns.

quiz.q: A prepositional phrase begins with a preposition and ends with a ___.
options: Noun or pronoun
A concept unrelated to prepositional phrases
Punctuation mark
Verb only

quiz.q: A fact is a statement that ___.
options: Can be proven true or false with evidence
Is always written in a persuasive tone
A concept unrelated to facts
Reflects only a personal belief or feeling

quiz.q: A prefix is added to the ___ of a word.
options: A position unrelated to prefixes
End
Beginning
Middle, always splitting the word in half

quiz.q: Recognizing a text’s structure pattern can help a reader ___.
options: A concept unrelated to text structure
Only understand the title of a text
Ignore the content of the text entirely
Better understand how ideas in the text are organized and connected

quiz.q: Why is it useful to review grammar, writing, and reading strategies together?
options: These skills have no connection to each other
It reinforces how these language skills connect and support one another
Review never helps strengthen understanding of language skills
A reason unrelated to reviewing language concepts

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Review: Math Days 61-69
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Math strand: this review lesson revisits key ideas from Days 61-69, including adding and subtracting decimals, nets of 3D figures, quadrilaterals, symmetry, and stem-and-leaf plots.

quiz.q: To add or subtract decimals correctly, you must first ___.
options: Round every number to the nearest whole number first
Line up the decimal points so digits match by place value
Ignore the decimal points completely
A step unrelated to adding decimals

quiz.q: A net is best described as ___.
options: A concept unrelated to nets
A three-dimensional figure with no flat faces
A type of graph used to display data
A two-dimensional pattern that folds into a three-dimensional figure

quiz.q: A rhombus is a quadrilateral with ___.
options: Only two equal sides
A description unrelated to a rhombus
No sides that are ever equal
Four equal sides

quiz.q: A shape has rotational symmetry if it ___.
options: Never looks the same no matter how it is turned
A concept unrelated to rotational symmetry
Looks the same after being turned less than a full rotation
Only looks the same after a full 360-degree turn

quiz.q: Why is it useful to review number, geometry, and data concepts together?
options: These topics have no connection to each other
Review never helps strengthen understanding of a subject
A reason unrelated to reviewing math
It reinforces how these math skills connect and build on one another

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: Review: Science Days 61-69
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Science strand: this review lesson revisits key ideas from Days 61-69, including animal adaptations, the Moon’s phases, gravity, conductors and insulators, and Earth’s atmosphere.

quiz.q: An adaptation is best described as ___.
options: A random change with no effect on survival
A concept unrelated to adaptations
A feature that always harms an organism’s chances of survival
A physical feature or behaviour that helps an organism survive in its environment

quiz.q: The Moon’s phases are caused by ___.
options: A concept unrelated to the Moon’s phases
The Moon changing shape physically each month
The Moon disappearing and reforming every month
Its changing position relative to Earth and the Sun

quiz.q: What keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun?
options: Strong winds in space
A concept unrelated to orbits
The complete absence of any force acting on the planets
The Sun’s gravitational pull

quiz.q: A conductor is a material that ___.
options: Blocks electric current from flowing through it
Has no connection to electricity at all
Allows electric current to flow through it easily
A concept unrelated to conductors

quiz.q: Why is it useful to review life systems, space, and physical science concepts together?
options: These topics have no connection to each other
It reinforces how these interconnected science concepts relate to one another
Each topic must be studied with no connection to the others
Review is never useful in science

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: Review: Social Studies Days 61-69
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Social Studies strand: this review lesson revisits key ideas from Days 61-69, including the Indus Valley Civilization, West African kingdoms, the French and American Revolutions, and levels of Canadian government.

quiz.q: The Indus Valley Civilization developed along which river system?
options: The Amazon River
The Nile River
A river unrelated to this civilization
The Indus River

quiz.q: The West African kingdoms of Ghana, Mali, and Songhai grew powerful largely through control of ___.
options: Gold and salt trade routes across the Sahara
A concept unrelated to these kingdoms
Trade routes that had no connection to gold or salt
Fishing rights along the Atlantic coast only

quiz.q: A major cause of the French Revolution was ___.
options: Widespread inequality and a financial crisis affecting the country
A concept unrelated to the French Revolution
An agreement between all social classes with no conflict
A period with no economic or social problems at all

quiz.q: Canada’s government is organized into which three levels?
options: A concept unrelated to Canada’s government structure
Regional, continental, and global
Only a single level, with no other divisions
Municipal, provincial, and federal

quiz.q: Why is it useful to review ancient civilizations, revolutions, and Canadian government together?
options: These topics have no connection to one another
Review is never useful when studying history
A reason unrelated to social studies learning
It reinforces how historical developments connect to how societies and governments are structured today

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Grammar: Adverbs and Adverbial Phrases
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Language strand: an adverb modifies a verb, adjective, or other adverb, often telling how, when, where, or to what extent something happens, and an adverbial phrase is a group of words serving the same function.

quiz.q: An adverb typically modifies a ___.
options: Noun or pronoun only
Punctuation mark
A concept unrelated to adverbs
Verb, adjective, or other adverb

quiz.q: Which word in the sentence “She sang beautifully” is the adverb?
options: Beautifully
Sang
A word unrelated to this sentence
She

quiz.q: Which of these adverbial phrases tells when an action happened?
options: Very quickly
After the bell rang
A phrase unrelated to adverbial phrases
Under the table

quiz.q: Many adverbs are formed by adding which suffix to an adjective?
options: -est
-ly
A suffix unrelated to forming adverbs
-ing

quiz.q: Why might a writer use an adverb such as “cautiously” instead of just “walked”?
options: A reason unrelated to adverbs
Adverbs can only describe nouns, never actions
Adverbs never add any detail to a sentence
It adds detail about how an action was performed

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Multiplying and Dividing Decimals by Powers of Ten
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Math strand: multiplying a decimal by a power of ten moves the decimal point to the right, while dividing by a power of ten moves the decimal point to the left, with the number of places matching the power’s exponent.

quiz.q: When you multiply a decimal by 10, the decimal point moves ___.
options: A direction unrelated to multiplying by ten
One place to the left
One place to the right
Two places to the right

quiz.q: What is 3.42 × 100?
options: A value unrelated to the calculation

quiz.q: What is 56.7 ÷ 10?
options: A value unrelated to the calculation
A value unrelated to the calculation

quiz.q: Why is it useful to recognize the pattern of moving the decimal point when multiplying or dividing by powers of ten?
options: It allows quick mental calculations without long multiplication or division
A reason unrelated to place value
Powers of ten have no effect on decimal numbers
This pattern never applies to decimal numbers

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: The Digestive System and Nutrient Absorption
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Science strand: the digestive system breaks down food into nutrients that the body can absorb and use for energy, growth, and repair, through organs including the stomach, small intestine, and large intestine.

quiz.q: The main purpose of the digestive system is to ___.
options: Filter air before it reaches the lungs
A concept unrelated to the digestive system
Break down food into nutrients the body can absorb and use
Pump blood throughout the body

quiz.q: Which organ mixes food with acid to begin breaking down proteins?
options: The lungs
An organ unrelated to digestion
The stomach
The heart

quiz.q: Most nutrient absorption into the bloodstream happens in the ___.
options: Large intestine
An organ unrelated to nutrient absorption
Esophagus
Small intestine

quiz.q: What is the main role of the large intestine in digestion?
options: Absorbing water and forming solid waste
A role unrelated to the large intestine
Breaking down proteins with acid
Pumping digested food to the heart

quiz.q: Why does the body need to break large food molecules into smaller nutrients during digestion?
options: Large food molecules are already able to enter cells directly
Smaller nutrient molecules can pass into the bloodstream and be used by cells
A reason unrelated to digestion
Breaking down food serves no useful purpose for the body

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: The War of 1812: Defending British North America
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Social Studies strand: the War of 1812 was fought between the United States and Britain (including its colonies in British North America), and its outcome helped shape a distinct identity for the colonies that would later become Canada.

quiz.q: The War of 1812 was fought primarily between Britain (with its colonies) and ___.
options: The United States
A country unrelated to the War of 1812
Spain
France

quiz.q: The War of 1812 took place in and around which region?
options: The Caribbean islands exclusively
Continental Europe
A region unrelated to the War of 1812
British North America (including present-day Ontario and Quebec)

quiz.q: Which group, alongside British soldiers and colonial militia, played an important role in defending British North America during the war?
options: Volunteers from countries outside North America only
A group unrelated to the War of 1812
No additional groups were involved in the defence
Indigenous allies, such as those led by Tecumseh

quiz.q: Why is the War of 1812 often seen as important to the development of a Canadian identity?
options: Successfully defending the colonies helped foster pride and a sense of shared identity
A reason unrelated to Canadian history
The war had no effect on the colonies’ sense of identity
The colonies were conquered and lost all self-governance

quiz.q: What was one major outcome of the War of 1812?
options: Britain lost control of all its remaining North American colonies
A concept unrelated to the war’s outcome
The United States permanently annexed all of British North America
Borders between British North America and the United States remained largely unchanged

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Writing: Procedural Writing — How-To Texts
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Language strand: procedural writing gives step-by-step instructions for completing a task, typically using a list of materials, sequential steps, and clear, imperative verbs.

quiz.q: Procedural writing is best described as ___.
options: Step-by-step instructions for completing a task
A story with characters and a setting
A poem describing personal feelings
A concept unrelated to procedural writing

quiz.q: Which of these sentences uses an imperative verb typical of procedural writing?
options: Flour, bowls, and pouring are sometimes related.
Pour the flour into the bowl.
The flour was poured into the bowl by someone.
A sentence unrelated to procedural writing

quiz.q: Why do procedural texts often include a list of materials at the beginning?
options: So the reader can gather everything needed before starting the steps
To make the text longer with no real purpose
A reason unrelated to procedural writing
Materials lists are never included in procedural writing

quiz.q: Which transition word would most likely appear in a procedural text to show order?
options: A word unrelated to sequencing steps
Meanwhile
Although
Next

quiz.q: Why is it important for the steps in a procedural text to be written in the correct order?
options: Following steps out of order could cause the task to fail or turn out incorrectly
Procedural texts are not meant to be followed in any specific order
A reason unrelated to procedural writing
The order of steps never affects the outcome of a task

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Angle Relationships: Complementary, Supplementary, and Vertical Angles
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Math strand: complementary angles sum to 90 degrees, supplementary angles sum to 180 degrees, and vertical angles are formed by intersecting lines and are always equal to each other.

quiz.q: Two angles are complementary if their measures add up to ___.
options: 180 degrees
A sum unrelated to complementary angles
90 degrees
360 degrees

quiz.q: Two angles are supplementary if their measures add up to ___.
options: A sum unrelated to supplementary angles
180 degrees
90 degrees
45 degrees

quiz.q: If one angle measures 35 degrees, what does its complementary angle measure?
options: 35 degrees
145 degrees
A measure unrelated to the calculation
55 degrees

quiz.q: Vertical angles, formed when two lines cross, are always ___.
options: Impossible to measure
Supplementary to each other
A relationship unrelated to vertical angles
Equal to each other

quiz.q: Why is understanding angle relationships useful when solving geometry problems?
options: Every angle in a diagram must be measured directly with a protractor
A reason unrelated to geometry
Angle relationships provide no useful information for solving problems
It allows missing angle measures to be calculated without a protractor

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: The Circulatory System: Heart, Blood, and Vessels
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Science strand: the circulatory system, made up of the heart, blood, and blood vessels, transports oxygen and nutrients throughout the body while carrying away waste products.

quiz.q: The main function of the circulatory system is to ___.
options: Transport oxygen, nutrients, and waste throughout the body
Break down food into nutrients
A concept unrelated to the circulatory system
Filter air before it reaches the lungs

quiz.q: Which organ pumps blood throughout the circulatory system?
options: The stomach
The heart
The liver
An organ unrelated to circulation

quiz.q: Which blood vessels carry oxygen-rich blood away from the heart to the body?
options: Capillaries only carry waste, never oxygen
Veins
Arteries
A vessel unrelated to circulation

quiz.q: What is the role of tiny blood vessels called capillaries?
options: Pumping blood directly out of the heart
Allowing oxygen and nutrients to pass between blood and body cells
Storing digested food for later use
A role unrelated to capillaries

quiz.q: Why is the circulatory system considered essential for nearly every cell in the body?
options: A reason unrelated to the circulatory system
The circulatory system only serves the heart itself
Most cells in the body do not need oxygen or nutrients
Cells rely on the blood supply for oxygen and nutrients to survive and function

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: The Underground Railroad and Its Connection to Canada
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Social Studies strand: the Underground Railroad was a secret network of routes and safe houses that helped enslaved people in the United States escape to freedom, with many settling in British North America (present-day Canada).

quiz.q: The Underground Railroad was best described as ___.
options: A concept unrelated to the Underground Railroad
A secret network of routes and safe houses helping enslaved people escape to freedom
A government program run openly by the United States
An actual railway built underground

quiz.q: Why did many freedom seekers travel all the way to British North America (present-day Canada)?
options: Canada offered no additional safety compared to the United States
A reason unrelated to the Underground Railroad
British North America required freedom seekers to remain enslaved
Slavery had been abolished there, offering greater safety and legal protection

quiz.q: People who helped guide freedom seekers along the Underground Railroad were sometimes called ___.
options: Passengers only, with no guides involved
A term unrelated to the Underground Railroad
Conductors
Engineers who built physical railways

quiz.q: Which of these communities in present-day Ontario became known as a settlement point for people who arrived via the Underground Railroad?
options: A community unrelated to the Underground Railroad
A settlement located outside of Canada
A city that refused to accept any new settlers
Buxton

quiz.q: Why is the story of the Underground Railroad an important part of Canadian history?
options: It highlights Canada’s role in offering freedom and safety to those escaping enslavement
The Underground Railroad had no connection to Canadian history
A reason unrelated to this history
No freedom seekers ever settled permanently in Canada

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Reading: Similes, Metaphors, and Personification
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Language strand: a simile compares two things using “like” or “as,” a metaphor states that one thing is another to suggest a comparison, and personification gives human qualities to something non-human.

quiz.q: A simile compares two things using which words?
options: Words unrelated to similes
Like or as
Because or therefore
Metaphor or simile

quiz.q: Which sentence is an example of a metaphor?
options: Her smile was sunshine on a cloudy day.
Her smile appeared briefly on her face.
A sentence unrelated to metaphors
Her smile was as bright as the sun.

quiz.q: Which sentence uses personification?
options: The wind blew at ten kilometres per hour.
The trees were tall and green.
The wind whispered through the trees.
A sentence unrelated to personification

quiz.q: Unlike a simile, a metaphor ___.
options: States directly that one thing is another, without using “like” or “as”
Always uses the word “like” to make a comparison
A description unrelated to metaphors
Never compares two different things

quiz.q: Why might an author use personification when describing a storm?
options: A reason unrelated to personification
Personification can only be used to describe human characters
Personification always makes writing harder to understand
It can make the storm feel more vivid, powerful, or alive to the reader

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Least Common Multiple and Greatest Common Factor
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Math strand: the least common multiple (LCM) is the smallest number that is a multiple of two or more numbers, while the greatest common factor (GCF) is the largest number that divides evenly into two or more numbers.

quiz.q: The least common multiple of two numbers is ___.
options: The largest number that divides evenly into both numbers
Always equal to one of the two original numbers
The smallest number that is a multiple of both numbers
A concept unrelated to least common multiple

quiz.q: What is the least common multiple of 4 and 6?
options: A value unrelated to the calculation

quiz.q: The greatest common factor of two numbers is ___.
options: The largest number that divides evenly into both numbers
A concept unrelated to greatest common factor
Always equal to one of the two original numbers
The smallest number that is a multiple of both numbers

quiz.q: What is the greatest common factor of 18 and 24?
options: A value unrelated to the calculation

quiz.q: Why is finding the greatest common factor useful when simplifying fractions?
options: Simplifying fractions never requires finding common factors
The greatest common factor has no connection to simplifying fractions
Dividing both the numerator and denominator by it reduces a fraction to lowest terms
A reason unrelated to fractions

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: The Respiratory System: Breathing and Gas Exchange
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Science strand: the respiratory system brings oxygen into the body and removes carbon dioxide, using the lungs as the main site of gas exchange between air and blood.

quiz.q: The main function of the respiratory system is to ___.
options: Pump blood throughout the body
Bring oxygen into the body and remove carbon dioxide
Break down food into usable nutrients
A concept unrelated to the respiratory system

quiz.q: Where does gas exchange mainly occur in the respiratory system?
options: In the heart’s chambers
In the stomach
A location unrelated to gas exchange
In tiny air sacs called alveoli, inside the lungs

quiz.q: When a person inhales, which gas mainly enters the bloodstream from the lungs?
options: Nitrogen is absorbed in the largest amount
Oxygen
Carbon dioxide
A gas unrelated to breathing

quiz.q: What role does the diaphragm play in breathing?
options: It pumps blood to the lungs
It contracts and relaxes to help air move in and out of the lungs
It filters food before it enters the stomach
A role unrelated to the diaphragm

quiz.q: Why is the respiratory system’s connection to the circulatory system important for the body?
options: Oxygen never needs to reach cells outside the lungs
A reason unrelated to these body systems
Oxygen absorbed by the lungs must be carried by the blood to cells throughout the body
The respiratory and circulatory systems have no connection to one another

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: Treaties and Indigenous-Crown Relations in Canada
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Social Studies strand: treaties are formal agreements made between Indigenous peoples and the Crown, historically involving land, resources, and rights, and they remain an important part of Indigenous-Crown relations in Canada today.

quiz.q: A treaty between Indigenous peoples and the Crown is best described as ___.
options: A formal agreement involving matters such as land, resources, or rights
A concept unrelated to treaties
A type of holiday celebrated across Canada
An informal conversation with no lasting effect

quiz.q: Why were many historical treaties in Canada focused on land?
options: Treaties in Canada have never mentioned land in any way
A reason unrelated to treaties
Land was never a topic addressed in Canadian treaties
They often set out how land would be shared or used by Indigenous peoples and settlers

quiz.q: Why is it important for treaties to be honoured by all parties involved?
options: Treaties represent legal and moral commitments that affect rights and relationships today
Only one side of a treaty is ever expected to follow its terms
Treaties have no legal or lasting significance once signed
A reason unrelated to treaties

quiz.q: Which of these best describes the ongoing relationship between Indigenous peoples and the Crown today?
options: A description unrelated to Indigenous-Crown relations
It ended completely once historical treaties were signed
It continues to evolve through dialogue, land claims, and treaty rights discussions
No relationship of any kind currently exists

quiz.q: Why do students study historical treaties as part of Canadian social studies?
options: Understanding treaties helps explain present-day rights, land use, and reconciliation efforts
Treaties have no connection to present-day Canadian society
A reason unrelated to studying Canadian history
Treaties are considered unimportant to Canadian history

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Vocabulary: Using a Thesaurus and Dictionary Effectively
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Language strand: a dictionary provides a word’s definition, pronunciation, and part of speech, while a thesaurus offers synonyms and antonyms to help writers choose more precise or varied words.

quiz.q: A dictionary is a resource that provides a word’s ___.
options: A concept unrelated to dictionaries
Only its spelling, with no other information
List of synonyms only, with no definitions
Definition, pronunciation, and part of speech

quiz.q: A thesaurus is most useful for finding ___.
options: Synonyms and antonyms for a word
The number of letters in a word
A concept unrelated to a thesaurus
A word’s exact pronunciation only

quiz.q: Why might a writer consult a thesaurus while revising a paragraph?
options: A thesaurus can only be used before any writing begins
A reason unrelated to using a thesaurus
To replace an overused word with a more precise or varied synonym
Thesauruses never provide alternative word choices

quiz.q: Which of these would most likely be found first in a dictionary entry?
options: A concept unrelated to dictionary entries
A list of the word’s antonyms only
A paragraph written entirely by the reader
The word’s pronunciation and part of speech

quiz.q: Why is it important to consider context when choosing a synonym from a thesaurus?
options: Not all synonyms carry the exact same tone or meaning in every situation
A reason unrelated to using a thesaurus
All synonyms for a word always mean exactly the same thing in every context
Context has no effect on which word is most appropriate

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Estimation Strategies for Multi-Step Problems
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Math strand: estimation strategies, such as rounding numbers before calculating, help predict a reasonable answer to a multi-step problem and check whether a final calculated answer makes sense.

quiz.q: Estimation in math is best described as ___.
options: Ignoring a problem entirely rather than solving it
A concept unrelated to estimation
Calculating an answer with complete precision every time
Finding an approximate, reasonable answer rather than an exact one

quiz.q: To estimate 297 + 512, which rounded numbers might you use?
options: A pair of numbers unrelated to this estimation

quiz.q: Why is estimation especially useful before solving a multi-step problem?
options: A reason unrelated to estimation
It helps predict a reasonable range for the final answer
Estimating makes multi-step problems impossible to solve
Estimation always provides the single, exact final answer

quiz.q: If you estimate an answer to be about 450, but your exact calculation gives 4,500, what does this suggest?
options: The exact calculation must be correct with no need to check further
Estimation is never useful for checking calculations
A calculation error likely occurred somewhere in the steps
A conclusion unrelated to estimation

quiz.q: Why might a shopper use estimation while adding up the cost of several items in a store?
options: It provides a quick check of whether they have enough money before reaching the checkout
A reason unrelated to estimation
Estimation provides no useful information while shopping
Shoppers are required to calculate exact totals mentally at all times

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: States of Matter and Changes of State
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Science strand: matter exists in states such as solid, liquid, and gas, and changes of state — like melting, freezing, evaporation, and condensation — occur when energy is added to or removed from a substance.

quiz.q: Which of these is a change of state that occurs when a solid becomes a liquid?
options: A process unrelated to changes of state
Condensation
Freezing
Melting

quiz.q: Which process describes a liquid changing into a gas?
options: Evaporation
A process unrelated to changes of state
Melting
Freezing

quiz.q: What generally happens to the particles in a substance as it is heated and changes from solid to liquid to gas?
options: They stop moving completely
A concept unrelated to particle movement
They lose energy and move closer together
They gain energy and move faster and farther apart

quiz.q: Condensation occurs when a gas ___.
options: Gains energy and changes into a solid
Loses energy and changes into a liquid
Remains a gas with no change occurring
A process unrelated to condensation

quiz.q: Why does water vapour on a cold glass of lemonade turn into visible droplets?
options: Water vapour never changes into liquid water
The glass produces new water that was not present before
The vapour loses heat energy near the cold surface and condenses into liquid water
A reason unrelated to changes of state

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: Social Studies: The Canadian Pacific Railway — Connecting the Country
subjects.summary: Grade 4 Social Studies strand: the Canadian Pacific Railway, completed in 1885, linked the country from coast to coast, encouraging settlement and trade, and helping fulfill a promise made to British Columbia when it joined Confederation.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Social Studies: The Canadian Pacific Railway — Connecting the Country

quiz.q: What did the Canadian Pacific Railway connect?
options: Nothing of importance
Communities from coast to coast across Canada
Canada to another country by land
Only two neighbouring cities

quiz.q: In what year was the Canadian Pacific Railway completed?
Why was building the railway important for British Columbia joining Confederation?
options: Canada promised a railway to connect BC to the rest of the country
The railway was built before BC existed
BC had no interest in railways
BC refused any transportation link

quiz.q: What did the railway help encourage across Canada?
options: Settlement and trade
The end of all trade
Fewer communities
Isolation between regions

quiz.q: What kind of workers helped build the railway, including through dangerous mountain sections?
options: Only government officials
No workers were needed
Only farmers
Labourers, including many Chinese workers

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Grammar: Coordinating and Subordinating Conjunctions
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Language strand: coordinating conjunctions (like “and,” “but,” and “or”) join equal ideas, while subordinating conjunctions (like “because,” “although,” and “since”) join a dependent clause to an independent clause.

quiz.q: Coordinating conjunctions are used to ___.
options: Join two equal ideas or clauses
Replace punctuation marks entirely
A concept unrelated to coordinating conjunctions
Only join a subject to a verb

quiz.q: Which of these is a coordinating conjunction?
options: Because
But
Although
A word unrelated to conjunctions

quiz.q: Which of these is a subordinating conjunction?
options: A word unrelated to conjunctions
Or
And
Because

quiz.q: In the sentence “Although it was raining, we went outside,” which word introduces the dependent clause?
options: Went
A word unrelated to this sentence
We
Although

quiz.q: Why might a writer choose a subordinating conjunction instead of simply joining two ideas with “and”?
options: Subordinating conjunctions must always come at the end of a sentence
Subordinating conjunctions never show a relationship between ideas
It can show a specific relationship, such as cause, contrast, or time, between the ideas
A reason unrelated to conjunctions

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Probability: Sample Space and Outcomes
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Math strand: a sample space is the set of all possible outcomes of an experiment, and probability compares the number of favourable outcomes to the total number of outcomes in that sample space.

quiz.q: The sample space of an experiment is best described as ___.
options: A concept unrelated to sample space
A single guaranteed outcome
The set of all possible outcomes
Only the outcomes that are considered favourable

quiz.q: What is the sample space when rolling a standard six-sided die?
options: A set unrelated to this sample space

quiz.q: If a bag contains 3 red marbles and 2 blue marbles, what is the probability of picking a red marble?
options: A probability unrelated to the calculation

quiz.q: When flipping a fair coin, what is the probability of landing on heads?
options: A probability unrelated to the calculation

quiz.q: Why is it useful to identify the full sample space before calculating a probability?
options: The sample space has no effect on calculating probability
Probability can be calculated accurately without knowing all possible outcomes
It ensures every possible outcome is accounted for when comparing favourable outcomes to the total
A reason unrelated to probability

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: Soil Composition and Formation
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Science strand: soil forms over long periods of time as rock is broken down by weathering and mixed with organic matter, water, and air, creating layers that support plant growth.

quiz.q: Soil is formed largely through the weathering of ___.
options: Only water, with no solid material involved
Rock, combined with organic matter over time
Metal objects buried underground
A concept unrelated to soil formation

quiz.q: Which of these is considered organic matter that can become part of soil?
options: A material unrelated to soil composition
Large boulders with no decomposition
Decomposed plant and animal material
Metal fragments from human structures

quiz.q: Why does soil formation typically take a very long time?
options: Weathering rock into small particles and mixing in organic material is a slow, gradual process
Soil requires no weathering or organic material to form
Soil forms instantly whenever rock is exposed to air
A reason unrelated to soil formation

quiz.q: Which layer of soil is typically richest in nutrients and organic matter, supporting plant growth?
options: Topsoil
A layer made entirely of ice
A layer unrelated to soil composition
Bedrock

quiz.q: Why is soil considered an important natural resource for ecosystems and agriculture?
options: It provides nutrients, water, and support that plants need to grow
Soil provides no benefit to plants or ecosystems
A reason unrelated to soil’s importance
Plants can grow equally well with no soil at all

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: The Fur Trade and the Voyageurs
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Social Studies strand: the fur trade was a major economic activity in early Canada, relying on voyageurs — skilled canoe travellers — and partnerships with Indigenous peoples to transport furs across vast distances.

quiz.q: The fur trade in early Canada was centred mainly around which resource?
options: Beaver pelts and other furs
Grain and other crops
Gold and silver
A resource unrelated to the fur trade

quiz.q: Voyageurs were best known for their skill in ___.
options: Paddling canoes over long distances to transport furs and goods
Building large stone structures
Farming large areas of land
A skill unrelated to voyageurs

quiz.q: Why were partnerships between European traders and Indigenous peoples important to the fur trade?
options: A reason unrelated to the fur trade
European traders required no assistance to succeed in the fur trade
These groups never worked together in the fur trade
Indigenous peoples had knowledge of the land, trapping, and trade routes essential to the trade’s success

quiz.q: Which companies competed for control of the fur trade in what is now Canada?
options: Only companies based outside of North America
The Hudson’s Bay Company and the North West Company
Companies unrelated to the fur trade
A single company that faced no competition at all

quiz.q: Why is the fur trade considered a significant part of early Canadian economic history?
options: A reason unrelated to the fur trade’s significance
It shaped exploration, trade routes, and relationships between European settlers and Indigenous peoples
The fur trade had no lasting effect on Canada’s development
The fur trade took place entirely outside of Canada’s territory

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Writing: Revising for Clarity and Conciseness
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Language strand: revising for clarity and conciseness means removing unnecessary words, combining repetitive ideas, and choosing precise language so that writing communicates its meaning as clearly as possible.

quiz.q: Revising for conciseness mainly involves ___.
options: Removing unnecessary words while keeping the meaning clear
Adding as many extra words as possible
A concept unrelated to conciseness
Rewriting a text in a completely different language

quiz.q: Which of these sentences is more concise while keeping the same meaning?
options: Homework dinner she quick finish before.
She quickly finished her homework before dinner.
A sentence unrelated to conciseness
She, in a very fast and quick manner, finished up completing all of her homework before the time came for dinner.

quiz.q: Why might a writer combine two repetitive sentences into one clearer sentence during revision?
options: A reason unrelated to revising for clarity
Combining sentences always makes writing more confusing
Repetitive sentences are always preferred over concise ones
It removes redundancy and helps the writing flow more smoothly

quiz.q: Which of these phrases could most likely be shortened for conciseness?
options: A phrase unrelated to conciseness
The dog ran
She smiled
Due to the fact that

quiz.q: Why is clarity an important goal when revising a piece of writing?
options: Clarity has no effect on how well a reader understands a text
Clear writing helps the reader understand the intended meaning without confusion
Confusing writing is always more effective than clear writing
A reason unrelated to revising writing

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Unit Rates and Comparing Best Buys
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Math strand: a unit rate expresses a quantity per single unit, such as price per item, and comparing unit rates helps determine which of two or more options offers the better value.

quiz.q: A unit rate expresses a quantity ___.
options: A concept unrelated to unit rates
As a fraction with no connection to a single unit
Per single unit, such as price per one item
Only in terms of time, never price

quiz.q: If 4 apples cost $2.00, what is the unit rate (price per apple)?
options: A rate unrelated to the calculation
$8.00 per apple
$2.00 per apple
$0.50 per apple

quiz.q: A box of 8 granola bars costs $4.00, and a box of 10 granola bars costs $4.50. Which box offers the better unit rate?
options: Both boxes offer exactly the same unit rate
A comparison unrelated to this calculation
The box of 10, at $0.45 per bar
The box of 8, at $0.50 per bar

quiz.q: Why is comparing unit rates more useful than comparing total prices alone when shopping?
options: It accounts for differences in quantity, showing which option is truly the better value
Unit rates provide no useful information for comparing prices
Total price always shows the better value regardless of quantity
A reason unrelated to comparing unit rates

quiz.q: If a car travels 240 kilometres in 3 hours, what is its unit rate of speed?
options: 60 kilometres per hour
A rate unrelated to the calculation
720 kilometres per hour
80 kilometres per hour

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: Freshwater and Saltwater Ecosystems
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Science strand: freshwater ecosystems, such as lakes and rivers, and saltwater ecosystems, such as oceans, support different communities of organisms adapted to their specific water conditions.

quiz.q: Which of these is an example of a freshwater ecosystem?
options: A saltwater coral reef
A concept unrelated to freshwater ecosystems
An ocean
A river

quiz.q: Which of these is an example of a saltwater ecosystem?
options: An ocean
A concept unrelated to saltwater ecosystems
A small freshwater pond
A freshwater lake

quiz.q: Why can most freshwater fish not survive if placed directly into a saltwater ecosystem?
options: Freshwater and saltwater fish always have identical adaptations
A reason unrelated to freshwater and saltwater ecosystems
Their bodies are adapted to a much lower salt concentration than ocean water contains
Freshwater fish are never adapted to any specific water conditions

quiz.q: Which of these organisms is specifically adapted to live in a saltwater ecosystem?
options: A frog living in a small freshwater pond
A clownfish living among ocean coral reefs
A trout living only in a freshwater stream
An organism unrelated to saltwater ecosystems

quiz.q: Why is it important for scientists to study both freshwater and saltwater ecosystems?
options: Only one type of water ecosystem exists on Earth
A reason unrelated to studying ecosystems
Each supports unique organisms and plays a distinct role in the health of the planet
Freshwater and saltwater ecosystems are identical, so studying both is unnecessary

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: Social Studies: The Klondike Gold Rush
subjects.summary: Grade 4 Social Studies strand: the Klondike Gold Rush of the late 1890s drew thousands of prospectors to the Yukon in search of gold, shaping the growth of towns such as Dawson City and the history of northern Canada.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Social Studies: The Klondike Gold Rush

quiz.q: What resource drew thousands of prospectors to the Yukon during the Klondike Gold Rush?
options: Gold
Diamonds
Oil
Coal

quiz.q: In which decade did the Klondike Gold Rush mainly take place?
options: The 1700s
The 1600s
The 1890s
The 1950s

quiz.q: Which town grew rapidly because of the Klondike Gold Rush?
options: Halifax
Ottawa
Toronto
Dawson City

quiz.q: What challenges did prospectors often face traveling to the Klondike?
options: Harsh terrain and difficult northern conditions
Easy travel by highway
Warm tropical weather
No challenges at all

quiz.q: How did the Klondike Gold Rush affect northern Canada?
options: It had no lasting effect
It caused the region to become empty
It only affected southern Canada
It brought rapid population growth and development to the region

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Reading: Mood and Atmosphere in Fiction
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Language strand: mood is the feeling or atmosphere a piece of writing creates for the reader, often shaped by word choice, setting, and descriptive imagery.

quiz.q: Mood in a story is best described as ___.
options: The exact number of characters in a story
The order in which events occur
A concept unrelated to mood
The feeling or atmosphere the writing creates for the reader

quiz.q: Which of these word choices would most likely create a mysterious mood?
options: Shadowy, silent, and eerie
Words unrelated to creating a mysterious mood
Loud, festive, and colourful
Bright, cheerful, and sunny

quiz.q: How does setting often contribute to a story’s mood?
options: Mood can only be created through dialogue, never setting
Setting has no connection to a story’s mood
A reason unrelated to mood
Details like weather, time, and location can shape how a scene feels to the reader

quiz.q: Which of these sentences most strongly creates a tense, suspenseful mood?
options: The floorboards creaked as a shadow moved slowly closer.
The book had two hundred pages.
The kitchen smelled like fresh cookies on a sunny afternoon.
A sentence unrelated to creating mood

quiz.q: Why might an author carefully choose descriptive imagery to build a story’s mood?
options: Strong imagery can immerse the reader in the emotional tone of a scene
Mood is entirely unaffected by an author’s descriptive choices
A reason unrelated to mood in fiction
Imagery has no connection to how a reader experiences a story’s mood

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Long Division with Multi-Digit Divisors
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Math strand: long division with a multi-digit divisor uses repeated steps of dividing, multiplying, subtracting, and bringing down digits to find a quotient, extending single-digit division strategies to larger numbers.

quiz.q: The steps of long division are generally repeated in which order?
options: An order unrelated to long division
Divide, multiply, subtract, bring down
Multiply, divide, bring down, subtract
Subtract, divide, bring down, multiply

quiz.q: What is 936 ÷ 12?
options: A value unrelated to the calculation

quiz.q: What is 1,244 ÷ 22?
options: A value unrelated to the calculation

quiz.q: When dividing 875 by 25, what does the remainder equal?
options: A remainder unrelated to the calculation
0, since 25 divides evenly into 875
5, since the division does not come out evenly
25, matching the divisor itself

quiz.q: Why is estimating a quotient first often helpful before completing long division with a multi-digit divisor?
options: Long division cannot be checked using estimation
It gives a reasonable range to check whether the final quotient makes sense
Estimating never provides useful information about a division problem
A reason unrelated to long division

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: Fossils and What They Reveal About Earth’s History
subjects.summary: Grade 6 Science strand: fossils are the preserved remains or traces of ancient organisms, and studying them helps scientists understand how life and environments on Earth have changed over millions of years.

quiz.q: A fossil is best described as ___.
options: A concept unrelated to fossils
A type of soil found only in deserts
A rock that has never contained any living material
The preserved remains or traces of an ancient organism

quiz.q: Fossils most commonly form when an organism is ___.
options: A process unrelated to fossil formation
Quickly buried by sediment that later hardens into rock
Placed underwater for only a few minutes
Left exposed to air and sunlight indefinitely

quiz.q: Why are fossils useful to scientists studying Earth’s past environments?
options: Fossils provide no information about past environments
A reason unrelated to fossils
All fossils are exactly the same age, regardless of location
They provide evidence of what organisms and conditions existed at a certain time

quiz.q: What can scientists learn by studying layers of rock that contain different fossils?
options: The exact weather conditions of the present day

subjects.subject: Math

subjects.subject: Language
